newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-COLOMBIA OVERCOME ALTITUDE TO DRAW WITH BOLIVIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COLOMBIA OVERCOME ALTITUDE TO DRAW WITH BOLIVIA.

text.p: Colombia, playing in the dreaded altitude of La Paz, came from behind twice to force a 2-2 draw with Bolivia on Sunday and keep their unbeaten record in the South American World Cup qualifying tournament.
Freddy Rincon, lucky not to be sent off for one particularly vicious foul, salvaged a point for Colombia when he scored with a superbly-placed shot in the 54th minute.
Rincon was the subject of a vendetta by Bolivian players after the first-half incident and was involved in several skirmishes with opponents.
For the second time in a row, Bolivia failed to make the most of the advantage of playing in La Paz, a nightmare venue for visiting teams because of its 3,600 metres altitude.
Colombia, with captain Carlos Valderrama in inspirational form, stayed top of the South American qualifiers with four wins and two draws.
Cold, driving rain made the pitch slippery and players took advantage to slide in recklessly on opponents. Peruvian referee Jose Arana booked seven players but overlooked numerous nasty incidents.
Bolivia went ahead in the 15th minute when defender Marcos Sandy rose above three opponents to score with a header.
Mauricio Serna equalised from a penalty, awarded for a foul on striker Faustino Asprilla, in the 40th minute.
Asprilla, scorer of six goals in Colombia's previous five games, made few other contributions and was substituted in the second half.
Striker Jaime Moreno scored a breathtaking individual goal to restore Bolivia's lead one minute before halftime.

Bolivia - 1-Carlos Trucco, 7-Fernando Ochoaizpur, 5-Oscar Sanchez, 2-Juan Manuel Pena, 3-Marco Sandy, 16-Luis Cristaldo, 20-Ramiro Castillo, 8-Milton Melgar (Vladimir Soria 70), 10- Marco Etcheverry, 18-William Ramallo (Milton Coimbra 75), 9- Jaime Moreno.

Colombia - 1-Farid Mongdragon, 13-Wilmer Cabrera, 5-Alexis Mendoza, 3-Jorge Bermudez, 17-Hugo Galeano, 14-Leonel Alvarez, 6-Mauricio Serna, 10-Carlos Valderrama, 19-Freddy Rincon (Andres Estrada, 75), 11-Faustino Asprilla (Luis Quinones 75), 7- Anthony de Avila (Juan Pablo Angel 87).
